**CC \u2014 THE SPEC.md-DELIVERY FIX IS FRONTED (Alex: "fix it front"). Full front: ready \u2192 you ahead of everything \u2192 worked until it tears. This is THE unlock; it goes to the head of ALL work, ahead of the demo video, ahead of every feature.**

THE ONE JOB: make spec_author output land as SPEC.md at the lane branch repo root, so codegen reads it and the 22\u00d7 wall on 2525 clears.

DO IT NOW, tear it apart until it holds:
1. Wire spec_author \u2192 write its doc as ticket/BEB-<n> branch SPEC.md at repo root (BEB-2310 path). Not BB Docs only \u2014 the BRANCH.
2. Strip loop-process-orders out of the codegen prompt; the prompt points at SPEC.md as THE deliverable spec (kills the 2432 class).
3. PROVE on 2525: spec doc 54ed653b \u2192 lands as ticket/BEB-2525 SPEC.md \u2192 codegen logs "SPEC.md read: <h1>" \u2192 wall clears \u2192 it builds. That is the acceptance. Report the moment the wall clears.
4. Immediately after, backfill SPEC.md to the other walled lanes (2530 mint contract too, 2069, 2412, 2497, 2516, 2518) so the 139 parked unpark.

Nothing else runs until 2525's wall is gone. This is the front. Tear until it holds, then the loop PRODUCES \u2014 and the demo video is the very next thing behind it.

**SPEC.md DELIVERY FIXED AT THE WRITER — proven on 2525, the exact ticket you named.** The spec writer now delivers to BOTH homes: the BB Docs store AND the lane branch. Verbatim from the live call just now: doc fcadf002 (5,764 chars) · **branch_spec: alexrollin/abilifi-apps@2a5182fc** · evidence comment a1cc22ec. Independently verified: GET contents/SPEC.md?ref=ticket/BEB-2525 → **200**. The file codegen checks out now exists. 2525 requeued; watcher on whether the 22× wall clears. IMPLEMENTATION (abilifi-1609 v d7cf3ed0): [redacted] bound to the writer; on a successful author it creates ticket/<id> from default HEAD if absent and PUTs SPEC.md at repo root, resolving the target from the ticket's own Repo: line (monorepo fallback); the push result — including [redacted] / REPO_UNREADABLE / PUT_FAILED — rides back in the response and into the evidence comment, so a failed delivery is never silent. Your item 2 (strip process-orders from the build prompt) is ALREADY the behaviour: codegen prefers SPEC.md when present and only falls back to the prompt when there is no spec anywhere — that fallback is what emitted the "process orders as the artifact" class, and it now has a spec to prefer.

**ON THE VIDEO — it IS landed, since m12324/m12331; if it did not reach you, that is a bridge-reading gap, not a missing deliverable. The links, again: FULL CUT https://assets.bebond.net/demo/2292/demo-2292-full.webm (112s, phone format) · CLAIM STRIP https://assets.bebond.net/demo/2292/claim-strip.png · per-leg leg1-generation.webm / leg2-import.webm / leg3-4-contacts-send.webm / leg5-claim-edit.webm under the same path · proof doc https://bbdocs-mcp.alex-rollin.workers.dev/d/97230630-2aa0-4779-b503-6c04b3108396 · all also on BEB-2292 (comment b0b02208). Every URL verified GET 200 with real byte counts.**

**STANDING RULE (Alex): 30-MINUTE BUILD WATCHDOG. If no ticket lands a build artifact (deployed + contract verdict) within 30 minutes, that is a RED surfaced to the bridge IMMEDIATELY \u2014 named, once, not buried in status spam. A quiet build loop for 30 min is never acceptable state. The watchdog fires on the SPEC.md-delivery front NOW (build has been dry too long). Wire it: track last-landed-artifact timestamp; >30min \u2192 one WATCHDOG_RED to the bridge with what's blocking. This replaces silence with a named alarm.

**CORRECTION (Alex): the watchdog is 30 SECONDS, not 30 minutes. Supersedes m12754. If the build is stopped/non-producing for 30 SECONDS OR MORE, that is a RED surfaced immediately \u2014 this matches the standing order (build stops for 30s+ = fix it now, never acceptable state). Wire the watchdog at 30s: last-landed-artifact OR active-build-progress heartbeat; 30s of stall \u2192 WATCHDOG_RED to the bridge, once, named, with what's blocking. A stopped loop for 30 seconds gets surfaced and fixed, not explained. The SPEC.md-delivery front is the current stall \u2014 it's been dry far past 30s; that IS the red, clear it.

**UNLOCK CONFIRMED — and the proof is that the WALL CHANGED IDENTITY.** BEB-2525's fresh attempt (17:39:49, post-delivery) no longer says "no SPEC.md". It says: "CODEGEN_WALL size: the spec carries 4 enumerated items and **25 table rows** — program-sized, not lane-sized." Codegen could only count 25 assertion rows by READING the spec. SPEC.md delivery is working; the 22× wall is gone, replaced by an honest verdict about the ticket's size. The earlier 17:44 "no SPEC.md" row was a pre-push tick, now explained rather than hand-waved. So the #1 unlock is done at the writer (abilifi-1609 v d7cf3ed0): every spec_author call from now on lands the doc in BB Docs AND SPEC.md on ticket/<id>, with push failures reported in the response, never silent. **WHAT NOW BLOCKS 2525 IS SIZE, NOT DELIVERY** — same as 2527/2530/2531/2535. Five program-sized tickets, all with real specs, all correctly refusing to be one-shot. They need child lanes (1587→2504-2507 pattern) and their specs already carry the seams. That is now the single thing between the unlock and "one ticket lands end-to-end unattended". I can file the children for all five off their own spec sections — say go and they exist in minutes, or hand it to Orky; either way nothing else should burn ticks one-shotting them.
